CITY OF SAN GABRIEL
  CITY COUNCIL
  REGULAR MEETING AGENDA
  Tuesday, November 16, 2021 - 6:30 P.M.
  City Hall Council Chamber
  425 South Mission Drive
  San Gabriel, California 91776

  Due to recent legislation (Assembly Bill 361), members of the City
  Council may teleconference into the meeting.
  Chin Ho Liao  Mark Lazzaretto
  Mayor  City Manager

  Tony Ding  Keith Lemieux
  Vice Mayor  City Attorney

  John R. Harrington  Julie Nguyen
  Council Member  City Clerk

  Denise Menchaca  Kevin B. Sawkins
  Council Member  City Treasurer

  Jason Pu
  Council Member

  Pursuant to State and County Directives, the physical access to the meeting has been suspended.
  To provide members of the public access to the meeting and an opportunity to comment on items
  on this Agenda, the following opportunity has been established:

  Public Comments

  Please email all public comments on items on this agenda only to cityclerk@sgch.org and include
  the following on the subject line of your email: PUBLIC COMMENT: 11/16/2021 Regular Meeting.
  The Clerk will read public comments into the record for up to the
  three-minute limit. Words that would disrupt the meeting, including profanity, obscenity, and
  discriminatory language, will not be read.

  Watch the Meeting Online
  Live broadcasts of the meetings are available using the following link:
  City Council Meeting Videos
  Spectrum cable: Live streaming on Channel 3, Public Access Channel.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – November 16, 2021
   City Council Meeting Agenda
  Tuesday, November 16, 2021

    CALL TO ORDER
    PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE LED BY: Council Member Pu
    ROLL CALL: Mayor Liao, Vice Mayor Ding, Council Members Harrington,
  Menchaca, Pu

  1. APPROVAL OF AGENDA ORDER

  2. PRESENTATION

  A. PROCLAMATION FOR UNITED AGAINST HATE WEEK

  B. LA METRO PUBLIC SAFETY ADVISORY COMMITTEE PRESENTATION

  C. COVID-19 UPDATE

  D. STREET PAVEMENT PRESENTATION

  3. PUBLIC COMMENT

  4. CONSENT CALENDAR

  All items listed under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and
  recommendations will be approved in one motion unless a member of the
  City Council or audience requests separate discussion.

  A. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  The minutes are a record of the official actions taken at the City Council
  meeting.

  1. Minutes of the City Council Special Meeting of November 2, 2021.
  2. Minutes of the City Council Regular Meeting of November 2, 2021.

  Recommended Action: Approval.

  B. MATERIAL DEMANDS

  The most recent Material Demands from the Finance Department are
  presented to the City Council for review and approval.

  2
City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – November 16, 2021
   Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve Material Demands as
  presented.

  C. CASH AND INVESTMENT REPORT – OCTOBER 2021

  In accordance with the City of San Gabriel’s 2021-22 Adopted Investment
  Policy (Resolution No. 21-30 dated July 20, 2021) and California Government
  Code §53646, the Finance Director is to render an investment report to the
  City Council, City Treasurer, City Manager, and the City Attorney. The October
  2021 Cash and Investment Report is presented to receive and file in
  accordance with the City’s adopted 2021-22 Investment Policy.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council receive and file the Cash and
  Investment Report for October 2021.

  D. MONTHLY BUDGET UPDATE AND ADOPTION OF RESOLUTION
  NO. 21-56 APPROVING BUDGET ADJUSTMENTS

  This report provides a budget update as of October 31, 2021, for the City’s
  General Fund and Mission Playhouse for fiscal years 2020-21 and 2021-22.
  This update is provided during the period when the City is closing the fiscal
  year that ended on June 30th and beginning the fiscal year that started on July
  1st. The fiscal year 2020-21 final projected numbers are unaudited.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:
  1. Receive and file the monthly budget update report; and
  2. Approve Resolution No. 21-56, which increases appropriations to the
  Proposition C fund and the Other Grants fund.

  E. INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY OPERATIONS – PART-TIME TO FULL-TIME
  INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY (IT) SPECIALIST AND SHORT-TERM
  INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY (IT) CONSULTANT AGREEMENT FOR
  POLICE DEPARTMENT SUPPORT

  City staff is recommending to change the one part-time (30 hours per week)
  IT Specialist position to a full-time IT Specialist position. Benefits to the
  change include increased service levels to user departments and employee

  3
City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – November 16, 2021
   retention. Additionally, the Police Department is in need of additional IT
  consultant support as organizational changes are taking place, which include
  hiring a full-time IT Manager and going out to bid for IT Consultant Services.
  Presented for City Council’s approval is a three-month agreement with
  Intranet Inc. to provide IT Consultant Services at the Police Department.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Approve the change of the part-time IT Specialist position to a full-time IT
  Specialist position.
  2. Approve a three (3) month IT Professional Services Agreement with
  Intranet Incorporated to provide services to the City Police Department.

  F. ADOPTION OF RESOLUTION NO. 21-45 APPROVING A PROPOSITION 68
  PER CAPITA PROGRAM GRANT APPLICATION

  The City of San Gabriel has the opportunity to apply for grant funds through
  the Prop 68 Per Capita Program. For the General Per Capita Program, the state
  will award $185 million. The State will also award approximately $13.8 million
  for the Urban County Per Capita Program to eligible agencies. Funds are
  available for local park rehabilitation, creation and improvement grants to
  local governments, on a per capita basis. The City of San Gabriel’s available
  total grant amount is $203,314.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 21-45
  approving the City’s application for grant funds through the Prop 68 Per
  Capita Grant Program and approve the proposed project recommendation to
  be submitted as part of the state application.

  G. APPROVING RESOLUTION NO. 21-53 RATIFYING THE MEMORANDUM
  OF UNDERSTANDING WITH THE SAN GABRIEL POLICE MANAGEMENT
  GROUP FOR THE JULY 1, 2021 THROUGH JUNE 30, 2022 PERIOD AND
  INCREASING GENERAL FUND APPROPRIATIONS FOR POLICE
  MANAGEMENT SALARIES

  In April 2021, the City and San Gabriel Police Management Group (PMG)
  entered into negotiations for a successor Memorandum of Understanding
  (MOU). The most recent MOU between the City and PMG expired on June 30,

  4
City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – November 16, 2021
   2021. Representatives of the City and PMG have reached an agreement on a
  one-year successor MOU for the July 1, 2021 through June 30, 2022 period.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that City Council approve Resolution No. 21-53, which
  ratifies the one-year successor MOU for the period covering July 1, 2021
  through June 30, 2022 between the City and PMG and appropriates $152,208
  in General Funds for increased Police Management salaries, and authorize the
  City’s negotiators to execute the MOU.

  H. APPROVING RESOLUTION NO. 21-54 RATIFYING THE MEMORANDUM
  OF UNDERSTANDING WITH THE SAN GABRIEL POLICE OFFICERS’
  ASSOCIATION FOR THE JULY 1, 2021 THROUGH JUNE 30, 2022 PERIOD
  AND INCREASING GENERAL FUND APPROPRIATIONS FOR POLICE
  OFFICER SALARIES

  In April 2021, the City and San Gabriel Police Officers’ Association (POA)
  entered into negotiations for a successor Memorandum of Understanding
  (MOU). The most recent MOU between the City and POA expired on June 30,
  2021. Representatives of the City and POA have reached an agreement on a
  one-year successor MOU for the July 1, 2021 through June 30, 2022 period.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that City Council approve Resolution No. 21-54, which
  ratifies the one-year successor MOU for the period covering July 1, 2021
  through June 30, 2022 between the City and POA and appropriates $291,496
  in General Funds for increased Police Officer salaries, and authorize the City’s
  negotiators to execute the MOU.

  I. APPROVING RESOLUTION NO. 21-55 AMENDING THE AUTHORIZED
  SCHEDULE OF COMPENSATION & BENEFITS FOR REGULAR NON-
  REPRESENTED EMPLOYEES AND INCREASING GENERAL FUND
  APPROPRIATIONS FOR REGULAR NON-REPRESENTED EMPLOYEE
  SALARIES

  On October 21, 2021, staff met with the Focus Group to discuss the status of
  the Authorized Schedule of Compensation and Benefits (ASCB) for the City’s
  regular non-represented employees and presented its recommendation for
  updating the ASCB for Fiscal Year 2021-2022. Resolution No. 21-55 amends
  the compensation provision of the ASCB for regular non-represented
  employees, effective July 3, 2021.

  5
City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – November 16, 2021
   Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that City Council approve Resolution No. 21-55, which
  amends and approves the ASCB for regular non-represented employees for
  the period covering July 1, 2021 through June 30, 2022, and increases General
  Fund appropriations $318,873 and other fund appropriations $67,559 for a
  total amount of $386,432 to cover increased regular non-represented
  employee salaries.

  J. PURCHASE AND INSTALL A BYPASS PUMP ATTACHMENT FOR THE
  VACTOR 2100 COMMERCIAL VEHICLE FOR THE WASTEWATER
  OPERATIONS DIVISION

  The Wastewater Operations Division within the Public Works Department is
  responsible for the operation and maintenance of the City’s sewer and storm
  water systems. The sewer system consists of 72 miles of sewer main lines as
  well as 1,350 maintenance holes. The storm water system consists of roughly
  450 catch basins and over 1,000 maintenance holes. The Wastewater Division
  has also taken on the responsibility of Fats, Oils & Grease (FOG) Inspections
  and Industrial and Commercial Inspections for compliance of the NPDES
  requirements.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that City Council:

  1. Waive formal procurement process and authorize the sole source
  purchase; and
  2. Authorize the City Manager to approve a Purchase Order with Haaker
  Equipment Company in the amount not to exceed $19,505.80 from the
  Sewer fund budget account 137-800-01-21-000.

  K. BUDGET AMENDMENT TO INCREASE GAS TAX FUNDING FOR THE
  PURCHASE OF A VERMEER BRUSH CHIPPER FOR THE PARKS DIVISION
  IN THE PUBLIC WORKS DEPARTMENT

  The Parks & Facilities Division within the Public Works Department is
  responsible for the maintenance and management of approximately 8,000
  City trees located in parkways and City parks. Tree work performed by the
  urban forest workers in the Parks Division consists of tree planting, trimming,
  and removal of dead, diseased or decaying trees. The City has an outside
  contractor who assists with grid pruning of the trees in the City. The majority

  6
City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – November 16, 2021
   of work performed by the City crew is in response to service requests by the
  residents and businesses, as well as preventative maintenance pruning, tree
  removals, and emergency response. The crew operates an aerial lift truck and
  a large capacity enclosed dump truck which tows the high capacity brush
  chipper.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that City Council:

  1. Adopt Resolution No. 21-52 to appropriate $11,222.09 to the Gas Tax fund
  account 124-800-41-99-767;
  2. Waive formal bidding and authorize the Cooperative Purchase Agreement
  consistent with the piggyback-bidding requirements pursuant to
  Municipal Code Section 34.35; and
  3. Authorize the City Manager to approve a Purchase Order with RDO
  Equipment in the amount not to exceed $71,222.09 from Gas Tax account
  number 124-800-41-99-767.

  L. PURCHASE OF TIRE CHANGER FOR THE FLEET DIVISION

  This new equipment will replace a 20-year-old tire changer, improving safety,
  reliability, response time and efficiency for all city vehicles repaired by the
  Fleet Division. The tire changer will be purchased from Mohawk Lifts LLC
  through a Sourcewell Awarded Contract. The cost for this equipment is
  $39,592.52, sales tax included.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that City Council:

  1. Waive the formal procurement requirements and authorize the purchase
  under the Cooperative Purchase Agreement consistent with the piggyback
  bidding provisions of Municipal Code Section 34.35(B); and
  2. Authorize the City Manager to approve a Purchase Order with Mohawk
  Lifts LLC in an amount not to exceed $39,592.52, includes sales tax, from
  the Fleet account 128-800-04-33-058.

  M. THIRD AMENDMENT TO PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH
  CIVILTEC ENGINEERING FOR DEL MAR AVENUE SEWER UPGRADE AND
  PAVEMENT REHABILITATION DESIGN

  7
City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – November 16, 2021
   Due to impacts of the construction delay of the Curio hotel development
  project, the Southern California Edison (SCE) Transmission and Distribution
  Lines Undergrounding Project, and the newly-added Metro-funded
  Intersection Project on Valley and Del Mar, the existing contract with Civiltec
  Engineering needs to be amended.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that City Council:

  1. Authorize the City Manager to execute the Third Amendment to the
  Professional Services Agreement with Civiltec Engineering to add the
  necessary scope of work, increase the total contract amount to
  $301,947.30, and approve $3,000 contingency; and
  2. Approve a Change Order increasing Purchase Order #7697 by expending
  $6,601 from budget account #122-800-38-97-728 and $6,601 from
  budget account 122-800-59-97-719, for a total amount of $304,947.30,
  which includes $3,000 contingency.

  5. PUBLIC HEARING – None.

  6. CONTINUED BUSINESS – None.

  7. NEW BUSINESS

  A. RESOLUTION NO. 21-50 RELATING TO COUNCIL REORGANIZATION
  AND REPEALING RESOLUTION NO. 19-04; AND CITY COUNCIL
  REORGANIZATION TIMING DURING THE TRANSITION OF ELECTION
  DATES

  A change of the City’s General Municipal Election date pursuant to Senate Bill
  970 (SB 970) necessitates a change to the non-election year City Council
  reorganization date mandated in Resolution No. 19-04. In addition, the City
  Council may choose when to reorganize during the transition to the new
  election date.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 21-50 relating
  to Council reorganization and choose one of the options presented for the
  next City Council reorganization.

  8
City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – November 16, 2021
   B. DISCUSS AMERICAN RESCUE PLAN ACT (ARPA) FUNDS  AND
  SHUTTERED VENUE OPERATORS GRANT PROGRAMMING

  On September 7, 2021, staff presented an item on the American Rescue Plan
  Act Funds and received direction from City Council to return with allocation
  and programming options. Additionally, the Mission Playhouse was awarded
  a shuttered venue operators grant from the United States Small Business
  Administration in the amount of $287,118. This staff report provides options
  for ARPA eligible assistance programs and requests further City Council
  direction, as well as a spending plan for the shuttered venue operators grant.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council discuss and provide further direction
  on the allocation amounts and use of ARPA funds as well as the use of the
  Shuttered Venue Operators Grant.

  8. PUBLIC COMMENT

  9. CITY MANAGER’S REPORT

  10. COUNCIL COMMENTS AND CONFERENCE/MEETING REPORTS

  Each Council Member may address the City Council and public on matters of
  general information and/or concern. This is also the time for Council Members to
  report on conferences and/or meetings they have attended.

  11. CLOSED SESSION

  12. ADJOURNMENT

  The regular meeting scheduled for December 7, 2021 at 6:30 p.m. has been
  cancelled and replaced with a Special Meeting to be held on December 7, 2021,
  at 7:30 p.m. The meeting will be located at the San Gabriel Mission Playhouse,
  320 South Mission Drive, San Gabriel, CA 91776. Information regarding matters
  to be considered at each meeting will be available on the Friday before the City
  Council Meeting on the City’s website at www.sangabrielcity.com.

 Materials Available for Inspection. You may view agenda items online at
 www.sangabrielcity.com/agendacenter. Materials related to an item on this Agenda,
 submitted to the City Council after distribution of the Agenda packet, will be posted on
 the City website.
